newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota lawmaker wants unicameral legislature.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota lawmaker wants unicameral legislature.

text.p: A Minnesota lawmaker said he plans to introduce a bill next week calling for a constitutional amendment to reduce the state legislature to a single chamber.
State Sen. David Kleis, R-St. Cloud, said the bill will mark his third attempt to get fellow lawmakers to put the proposed amendment for a unicameral legislature on the ballot.
Kleis pointed out that while Minnesota ranks 21st in population among the states, its legislature is the fourth largest with 67 senators and 134 representatives.
His proposal would create a single legislative chamber of 135 lawmakers.
Kleis said the move, supported by Gov. Arne Carlson, would save the state about $66 million every two years.

Unlike his previous two attempts, Kleis said he was forming a state-wide organization to educate voters on his proposal. He said he is aiming his bill, which requires a simple majority vote of each legislative chamber, for the 1998 or 2000 general election ballot.
Nebraska is the only state with a unicameral legislature.
